input_signals.name: Unjustified-Discount Gap
input_signals.expression: SUB(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(lt, at), NEG(MA(RATIO(ib, at), 3)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Within an industry, the part of a firm's cheapness that is not matched by its distress ranking is mispricing; the part that is matched is fair compensation for default risk.
input_signals.reasoning: Differencing the industry rank of book-to-market against the industry rank of a fundamental distress score (leverage plus smoothed three-year profitability) yields an explicit residual-discount measure, so the signal is large only when a firm is cheap without a distress justification. Industry ranking removes sector-level leverage norms and multiple levels that would otherwise drive the spread.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( ind_rank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), ind_rank( sumrank( ratio( lt, at ), neg( ma( ratio( ib, at ), 3 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Weakest-Link Cheap and Debt-Serviceable
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(oancf, dlc), lt)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The value premium is conjunctive rather than additive: a firm must be both cheap and able to cover its liabilities out of internally generated cash after current maturities, and failing either condition destroys the premium entirely rather than partially offsetting it.
input_signals.reasoning: MIN replaces the fixed-weight rank blend with a non-substitutable (Leontief) interaction, so a very high book-to-market can no longer compensate for weak debt-service capacity the way it does in a Piotroski-style additive score. The distress channel is a flow-versus-stock coverage measure, (oancf - dlc)/lt, rather than a leverage level, and firms with negative book equity or negative post-maturity cash flow are correctly pinned to the short leg.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( winsor( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( ratio( sub( oancf, dlc ), lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: Repaired-Balance-Sheet Cheapness
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_RANK(SUB(TS_MAX(RATIO(lt, at), 5), RATIO(lt, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cheap firms whose leverage now sits far below its own five-year peak have completed a balance-sheet repair that removed the default risk originally responsible for the discount, but the discount persists because investors anchor on the prior distressed state.
input_signals.reasoning: Distance from a firm's own leverage maximum is a within-firm recovery measure that is not a cross-sectional quality score, so it should not be absorbed by RMW or CMA the way the failed healthy-cheapness composites were. This is the constructive counterpart to the trap signals: it asks whether the positive polarity can work at all once the healthy leg is defined by distress *resolution* rather than by static financial strength.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), ind_rank( sub( ts_max( ratio( lt, at ), 5 ), ratio( lt, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cheap Post-Distress Turnaround
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), MUL(INDICATOR(RATIO(pi, at), 0), IND_RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(NEG(ib), 0), 5))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cheap firms that have just returned to pretax profitability after a multi-year loss run are still priced on their distressed history; investors extrapolate the loss record, so the resolution of distress is under-reacted to and produces positive abnormal returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The failed positive-polarity attempts all defined the healthy leg by *static* strength, which FF5's RMW and CMA already price; here the long leg requires a documented loss history plus a current profit, a state variable no factor spans. Firms still losing money receive zero and fall to the bottom of the sort, which is economically the correct short leg rather than an arbitrary neutral block.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), mul( indicator( ratio( pi, at ), 0 ), ind_rank( ts_sum( indicator( neg( ib ), 0 ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Tax-Validated Cheapness
input_signals.hypothesis: Cash-tax expense is a costly, externally verified confirmation that reported profits are real; a cheap firm paying a normal effective tax rate has earnings the tax authority believes in, whereas a cheap firm with negligible or negative tax expense is either losing money or sheltering behind loss carryforwards accumulated in past distress.
input_signals.reasoning: The effective tax rate is close to scale-free and largely orthogonal to the profitability *level* that RMW prices, which is why it is a candidate for the positive polarity that static quality composites have failed to deliver; it also uses the tax channel, untested anywhere in the archive. Loss-making and NOL-sheltered firms fall naturally to the bottom of the second rank, so the short leg is cheap firms whose reported earnings carry no tax validation.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), ind_rank( winsor( ratio( txt, pi ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Long-Dated Liability Cheapness
input_signals.hypothesis: Holding the size of the claim load fixed, *when* it falls due determines whether a cheap firm can work through its problems; firms whose liabilities are predominantly long-dated have breathing room, so their discount is not a distress discount and should revert.
input_signals.reasoning: This abandons the net-net floor logic entirely and replaces it with liability maturity structure, a dimension of the distress theme the archive has never tested — every prior distress leg measured the amount, the trajectory, or the volatility of claims, never their timing. It also avoids the failure mode of previous positive-polarity attempts because a low current-liability share is not a profitability or asset-growth characteristic, so RMW and CMA have little reason to span it.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( lct, lt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Centered Fragility Among Cheap Firms
input_signals.hypothesis: The economically interesting comparison is between cheap fragile and cheap robust firms; with severity centered rather than ranked, magnitude comes from cheapness and sign from fragility, so the short leg is cheap-and-fragile and the long leg is cheap-and-robust rather than expensive-and-robust.
input_signals.reasoning: This isolates one design choice — centering the severity leg — to fix the diagnosed reason our trap spreads have near-zero Sharpe despite reliable negative alpha: the low leg is currently a glamour basket whose raw return offsets the trap gain, and both legs should instead sit in the cheap tail so HML exposure largely cancels. Unlike the earlier within-cheap attempts, there is no indicator gate, so no zero block contaminates the extreme deciles and coverage is unchanged.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( sale, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), ind_zscore( neg( ts_min( ratio( pi, at ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Value Premium Inside the Fragile Group
input_signals.hypothesis: Holding fragility fixed, price does the discriminating: among firms with demonstrated deep-loss capacity, the cheaply priced ones are compensated for bearing that risk while the richly priced ones are lottery tickets, so the spread between cheap-fragile and dear-fragile firms should be positive.
input_signals.reasoning: This is the mirror decomposition of the accepted "Compensated Distress Inside Value" — that signal fixes cheapness and varies distress, this one fixes fragility and varies price — so the pair localises which dimension carries the interaction, and neither is a rank complement of an archived expression because the signed z-score makes the signal non-monotone in both themes. Magnitude is set by fragility and sign by valuation, so both extreme legs sit in the fragile tail and the spread is distress-neutral by construction rather than a restatement of expensive-junk underperformance.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( neg( ts_min( ratio( pi, at ), 5 ) ) ), ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( sale, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Dear with Weak Claim Coverage
input_signals.hypothesis: A premium multiple is only defensible if the business generates enough operating profit to service the claims standing ahead of equity; among richly valued firms, those whose EBITDA is small relative to total liabilities are paying creditors out of future promises, while their well-covered peers at the same multiple are genuine franchises.
input_signals.reasoning: This retains the centered structure that produced the archive's largest alpha but changes the economic content of the severity leg from the *stock* of net debt to the *flow* coverage of all claims, so it is not a one-operator respecification and it does not reintroduce a monotone expensiveness main effect — both extreme portfolios remain inside the expensive tail. It also tests corner dependence directly: the same coverage channel was nearly worthless in the cheap tail (−0.6%, t=−0.57), so a large alpha here would establish that claim coverage matters only where the market has already paid a premium.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( mul( prcc_f, csho ), sale ) ), ind_zscore( neg( winsor( ratio( ebitda, lt ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Dear with Either Risk Realised
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(MUL(prcc_f, csho), sale)), MAX(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(lt, che), at), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(TS_MIN(RATIO(pi, at), 5)), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: A premium valuation can be destroyed by either route — creditors holding a large net claim or a demonstrated capacity for deep operating losses — and being clean on one route provides no offset, so the worst of the two standardised risks is what should price the equity.
input_signals.reasoning: MAX over two z-scored risks implements the union logic the hypothesis actually states, replacing the rank-average that merely blended two documented main effects, and because both risk inputs are centered the low leg consists of expensive firms exposed to neither risk rather than of cheap firms. The two routes are economically distinct — one balance-sheet stock, one income-statement tail — so the union should broaden the short leg from the rare firms extreme on both to every premium-valued firm exposed on either, which is the route to a more reliable alpha t-statistic.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( mul( prcc_f, csho ), sale ) ), max( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( lt, che ), at ), 1 ) ), ind_zscore( winsor( neg( ts_min( ratio( pi, at ), 5 ) ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Sustained Premium with Either Risk
input_signals.expression: MUL(MA(IND_RANK(RATIO(MUL(prcc_f, csho), sale)), 5), MAX(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(lt, che), at), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(TS_MIN(RATIO(pi, at), 5)), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: A multiple the market has sustained for five years is a capitalised narrative rather than a transient re-rating, and when such a firm is exposed to either creditor claims or deep-loss capacity the eventual disappointment is larger than for a firm whose premium is new.
input_signals.reasoning: The persistence idea produced the archive's largest alpha (−4.8%, t=−4.74) but a dead slope because the valuation leg was an integer occupancy count; replacing it with a five-year moving average of the expensiveness rank keeps the same economics as a smooth, monotone quantity. Pairing it with the union severity that fixed the slope in gen 8 is the single most promising combination the run has identified, and it is a construction repair rather than a new mechanism by design.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ma( ind_rank( ratio( mul( prcc_f, csho ), sale ) ), 5 ), max( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( lt, che ), at ), 1 ) ), ind_zscore( winsor( neg( ts_min( ratio( pi, at ), 5 ) ), 1 ) ) ) )
